advisory.checklist_item: - [ ] Make the lightweight-tag guard check the properties that actually make the tag lightweight (gh release create with --target, no --verify-tag, no git/tags API call), not just the absence of `git tag -a`.
evidence: tests/unit/test_release_workflow_pins.py (added): `assert "git tag -a" not in _text(), "release.yml now creates annotated tags; fix the doc"`
.github/workflows/release.yml:304-305: `Without `--verify-tag`, `gh` creates the lightweight dispatch-version tag at the authorized run SHA.`
.github/workflows/release.yml:299-303: the github_release job's steps are only download-artifact and the gh step, with no actions/checkout, so a local `git tag` could not run there anyway
advisory.finding: The new guard in test_docs_tag_type_matches_workflow only checks that the literal substring `git tag -a` is absent from release.yml. The github_release job has no checkout, so `git tag -a` is the least likely way it would ever make an annotated tag. More likely routes are `gh api .../git/tags` (create a tag object) followed by `gh release create --verify-tag`, or `git tag --annotate`/`-s`/`-m`. The test would pass on all of these while the doc is wrong again. A missing substring here cannot tell 'still lightweight' apart from 'annotated by some other route'.
scenarios: A later change adds `gh api repos/$GH_REPO/git/tags -f tag=... -f message=...` plus `gh api .../git/refs` and switches to `gh release create --verify-tag`; the tags become annotated, the test still passes, and docs/releasing.md is wrong again.
advisory.suggested_fix: In the test, assert on the github_release run text directly: `assert "--target" in run`, `assert "--verify-tag" not in run`, `assert "git/tags" not in run`, and `assert not re.search(r"git tag\s+(-a|--annotate|-s|--sign|-m)", _text())`.

advisory.checklist_item: - [ ] Pin the lightweight-tag mechanism in test_docs_tag_type_matches_workflow: assert `--target "$SHA"` is in the create line, `--verify-tag` is absent, and there is no `git tag` / `git/tags` API call anywhere in release.yml.
evidence: tests/unit/test_release_workflow_pins.py (added): `assert "gh release create" in run` and `assert "git tag -a" not in _text(), "release.yml now creates annotated tags; fix the doc"`

Comment at .github/workflows/release.yml:304-305 says the tag is lightweight only because `--verify-tag` is not passed: "Without `--verify-tag`, `gh` creates the lightweight dispatch-version tag at the authorized run SHA."

The command at .github/workflows/release.yml:323 is `gh release create "$TAG" --target "$SHA" --title "$TAG" --generate-notes --latest dist/*`; the test asserts neither `--target` nor the absence of `--verify-tag`.
The doc text added in this diff (docs/releasing.md) promises `gh release create "v<version>" --target <released SHA>`, but the test never checks `--target`.
Added assertion: `assert "### Tag signing — SKIPPED (lightweight tags + attestations instead)" in doc`
docs/releasing.md is human-facing prose. Nothing in the diff shows a parser or other tool that reads this exact heading string.

For comparison, the absence checks (`"keep **annotated** tags" not in doc`, the two stale RC phrases) already guard against the old wrong claims. The heading check adds wording-pinning, not much extra protection.
advisory.finding: The workflow half of the test can't catch most ways release.yml could start creating annotated tags or tagging something other than the released SHA. It only checks that the literal string `git tag -a` is absent and that `gh release create` is present. It doesn't check `--target`, doesn't check that `--verify-tag` is absent, and doesn't catch other ways to make an annotated tag.
merged_from: The test requires the doc heading to match word for word, including the em dash and capitalization. That pins prose that only people read, so rewording the heading breaks the test even if the doc still says tags are lightweight.
scenarios: Someone adds a step `git tag -m "Release v$VERSION" "v$VERSION" && git push origin "v$VERSION"` (or `git tag --annotate ...`, or `gh api repos/$GH_REPO/git/tags -f tag=...`) and switches the create call to `gh release create "$TAG" --verify-tag ...`. The tags are now annotated, but the test passes because the literal `git tag -a` never appears.
`--target "$SHA"` is dropped. gh then tags the default-branch HEAD instead of the released SHA, which contradicts the doc, and the test stays green.
advisory.suggested_fix: Replace the `git tag -a` check with: `create = next(l for l in run.splitlines() if "gh release create" in l); assert '--target "$SHA"' in create and "--verify-tag" not in create; assert not _re.search(r"git\s+tag\b|/git/tags", _text())`.
